title: SASSA Child Support Grant: 2026 Rules
description: SASSA Child Support Grant: who qualifies, the R580 monthly amount, documents, how to apply, payment dates, and what to do if an approved grant is not paid.
author: Lucky Cungwa

sections.title: What is the SASSA Child Support Grant?
sections.content: The SASSA Child Support Grant is a monthly payment to the primary caregivers of children under 18 who live in low-income households. It is the most widely distributed grant in South Africa, reaching millions of children each month. As of 2026, the grant amount is {{child_support_grant_amount}} per child per month. The grant is intended to help cover the costs of raising a child, including food, clothing, school supplies, and healthcare. Unlike the SRD grant, this is a permanent grant that continues as long as you meet the eligibility criteria.

sections.title: Eligibility Requirements
sections.content:
To qualify for the SASSA Child Support Grant in 2026, you must meet the following requirements:
  • Primary caregiver: You must be the person who takes primary responsibility for meeting the child's daily needs. This can be a parent, grandparent, guardian, or foster parent.
  • Income threshold: Your income (as the primary caregiver) must not exceed {{child_support_income_threshold_single}} per month if single, or {{child_support_income_threshold_married}} per month combined if married.
  • Child's age: The child must be under 18 years old.
  • Citizenship: You and the child must be South African citizens, permanent residents, or refugees.
  • Means test: SASSA will assess your income and assets to determine if you qualify.

sections.title: Required Documents
sections.content:
You need the following to apply for the Child Support Grant:
  • Your 13-digit ID (green ID book or smart ID card)
  • Child's birth certificate (unabridged version preferred)
  • Child's 13-digit ID number (if they have one)
  • Proof of income — payslips, bank statements, or an affidavit if you have no income
  • Proof of residence — utility bill or affidavit
  • School report or clinic card (if the child is of school age)
  • Affidavit from the biological parent (if you are not the child's parent)

steps.title: Start Your Application (Online or In Person)
steps.content: You can start your Child Support Grant application online via the official SASSA Services Portal at services.sassa.gov.za — register, log in, and complete the online application. Alternatively, apply in person at a SASSA office. Locate your nearest office on our resources page.

steps.title: Bring the Child and All Documents
steps.content: It is recommended that you bring the child with you, though an application can be made without the child if you have the required documents.

steps.title: Complete the Application
steps.content: A SASSA officer will assist you with the application form. Provide accurate information about your income and living situation.

steps.title: Keep Your Receipt
steps.content: You will receive a receipt with a reference number. This is your proof of application.

steps.title: Wait for Approval
steps.content: Processing can take up to 3 months. You will receive an SMS notification once your application is approved or declined.

sections.title: Payment Dates, Amount and Late Payments
sections.content: The Child Support Grant amount is {{child_support_grant_amount}} per child per month in 2026. It is paid on the children's grant payment day, which normally falls in the first week of each month; SASSA can move a cycle when a public holiday falls inside the payment window. Always confirm the current month's date on the SASSA payment calendar rather than relying on an old date. If you have more than one qualifying child, you receive the amount for each child, paid to the primary caregiver rather than to the child. If your application shows Approved but the money has not arrived, allow 1 to 3 business days after the payment date, then follow the missing grant payment guide. If the status says Bank Details Pending, fix the banking details first using the bank details guide.

faqs.q: Can I get the Child Support Grant if I am working?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as your monthly income is below the threshold. Many working parents qualify because the threshold is higher than the SRD grant.

faqs.q: What happens when the child turns 18?
faqs.a: The grant stops when the child turns 18. You must inform SASSA of the child's birthday to avoid being asked to repay any overpayments.

faqs.q: Can a grandmother apply for the Child Support Grant?
faqs.a: Yes, grandparents who are the primary caregivers of their grandchildren can apply. You will need to provide an affidavit explaining the circumstances.

faqs.q: Can I apply for the Child Support Grant online?
faqs.a: Yes. You can start your application online via the official SASSA Services Portal at services.sassa.gov.za. You may still need to visit a SASSA office to submit supporting documents.

faqs.q: Can I receive the grant for a child who is not my biological child?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are the primary caregiver of the child. You will need to provide documentation showing your relationship to the child and the circumstances of your care.

faqs.q: When is the Child Support Grant paid each month?
faqs.a: Children's grants are normally paid in the first week of the month, on the children's grant payment day. The exact date can move when a public holiday falls in the payment window, so check the current month on our SASSA payment calendar or your own status rather than using an old date.

faqs.q: My Child Support Grant was approved but I have not been paid. What should I do?
faqs.a: First check whether your status shows a payment date and whether it says Bank Details Pending. If the payment date has passed, allow up to 3 business days for the bank transfer to reflect. If the money still has not arrived, follow our missing grant payment guide and contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 with your ID number and reference number.

faqs.q: How do I check my Child Support Grant status?
faqs.a: You can check your status at a SASSA office, by phoning 0800 60 10 11, or through the official SASSA channels. Your grant is not an SRD grant, so the SRD portal status check does not show it. Keep your receipt and reference number from the application.

sections.title: Child Support Grant Top-Up for Orphaned Children
sections.content: Children who are orphaned, in child-headed households, or whose caregiver cannot be traced may qualify for the Child Support Grant top-up, an additional monthly amount paid on top of the standard grant. The top-up amount has changed over the years and is set in each national budget, so the exact total depends on the top-up in effect at the time. Check the current amount with SASSA (0800 60 10 11) or on the official sassa.gov.za website before budgeting on a specific figure. A caregiver can apply for this top-up through the normal SASSA channels by stating that the child is orphaned or abandoned.
